text:
marta: Heads up — after yesterday's bulk RBAC refactor, compliance asked for a proof of who changed org-level roles. Our audit export has ~200 events where actor == null. Anyone else seeing missing provenance?

josh: Seeing NULL actor in audit_stream for action=role.assign and role.update. Quick grep shows `actor` is literally null in the DB rows. Suspect the migrator job ran with a service account that didn't set performed_by header. :thinking_face: 

audit-bot: ingest: 2025-12-03T14:12:23Z event_id=evt-7f3c actor=null action=role.update resource=org/123 

sylvia: @josh can you paste the migrator job command / pod annotations? We rotated KMS keys last week so need to check token provenance. :eyes: 

josh: job YAML snippet I found in k8s: `kubectl apply -f rbac-migrator-job.yaml` env: `EXECUTOR=service-agent` image: `gcr.io/redwood/rbac-migrator:v2.1.0` — I don't see performed_by env var. Relay header showed `x-requested-by: migrator` only. 

nate: Note: our relay intentionally drops actor if the signed assertion can't be validated against the active KMS key to avoid recording possibly forged principals. That behavior was added during the KMS rotation to be conservative. But dropping to null is painful for audits; we should tag origin=unattributed instead. 

marta: Compliance wants an action plan: can we backfill actors for those ~200 events? If yes, how reliable will mappings be? Also need a timeline for fixing the relay. 

josh: We do have kube job annotations and pod logs with `started_by`/`jenkins` metadata. The audit payloads include `session_id` which matches an annotation. We can join on session_id -> pod annotation -> started_by. Example log snippet: 
```json
{
  "event_type": "role.update",
  "event_id": "evt-7f3c",
  "actor": null,
  "session_id": "sess-abc123",
  "annotations": {"kube_started_by": "jenkins/job/789", "git_commit": "c4f3b2"},
  "raw_blob": "..."
}
``` 
This suggests good join keys for backfill. 

sylvia: Good catch. I'll write a backfill script to populate `actor` using session_id -> kube annotations. We need a DB policy: legal ok'd updates if we record an `original_actor_null` flag and keep original raw_event blob. Can we add that metadata column? 

marta: Yes, compliance requires preserving original raw_event and marking any reconstructed actor with proof links. Also open a ticket to change relay behavior: when a signed assertion is present but KMS key id mismatches, set actor = `service:<key-id>` plus origin=signature_mismatch instead of null. 

josh: Created PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/relays/pulls/456 — adds fallback actor tag and emits `relay.provenance` details in audit. PTAL @sylvia :+1: 

sylvia: Will review today. Also adding a monitor: alert if count(audit.actor == null) > 5 per minute to avoid future silent batches. Page owner SRE. 

audit-bot: alert: audit-null-actor rate=12/min last5m threshold=5/min triggered 

nate: Forensics note: pattern matches deploy window 2025-12-03T13:00-14:30 and correlates with k8s job runs. No signs of malicious tampering — looks like ops/config gap. Recommend post-mortem with SRE, relays, and dev-ex. 

marta: Agree. I'll draft the incident summary and include backfill plan, PR link, and the monitoring rule. Will schedule post-mortem. :calendar:
